data: seeded demo data, scripted `test` provider, no keys, no network, HOME and data dir under a temp folder

shots.caption: Plan mode: the agent proposes a plan, one line per step with the tool it will use. Edit it, then Execute.
shots.alt: Cortex chat in Plan mode showing an editable three-step plan with tool chips for file-read, before it is executed.

shots.caption: After Execute, each plan step runs and the to-do list ticks off as it finishes.
shots.alt: Cortex chat after a plan was executed: the agent's reply above and the to-do list below showing all three steps checked off.

shots.caption: A durable run you stopped keeps its place. Continue resumes the same run without repeating finished work.
shots.alt: Cortex chat showing 'Stopped by you' with the tool already done, an optional note for the agent, and a Continue button.

shots.caption: Tools Lab: MCP servers with live connection status and each tool's input schema.
shots.alt: Cortex Tools Lab listing three MCP servers: two connected with their tools, one failed with its error.

shots.caption: The same Tools Lab at a narrow width.
shots.alt: Cortex Tools Lab at 600 pixels wide, MCP servers stacked in one column.

shots.caption: Channels hub: Telegram, Signal and webhook channels, the agent each one routes to, and who may talk to it.
shots.alt: Cortex channels hub with three channels, their routes to a saved agent, and access settings.

shots.caption: Beacon, the first view of a new Cortex: the neural mark with calm sonar rings while it waits for your first agent.
shots.alt: Cortex Beacon first-run view: the neural mark in the middle of the page, 'Welcome to Cortex', and buttons to open a chat, build an agent or connect an app.
shots.note: Motion on; every CSS animation is paused at 2.0 s so the frame is the same on every run. beacon-still is the reduced-motion version.

shots.caption: The same Beacon view with reduced motion: the neural mark at rest.
shots.alt: Cortex Beacon first-run view with the neural mark at rest and no animation.
shots.note: prefers-reduced-motion emulation; animations disabled at capture.

shots.caption: Lab builder: set the model and tools on the left, name the agent and run it from the panel on the right.
shots.alt: Cortex Lab builder with the Model section open and the Run this agent panel showing the name, task, a summary, and the Save and run and Save buttons fully visible.

shots.caption: Lab, Reliability: learned and community calibration are two switches, both off until you turn them on.
shots.alt: Cortex Lab builder Reliability section with the Learned calibration and Community calibration checkboxes both unchecked and a note that they are off by default.

shots.caption: Lab, Execution: durable runs are on by default in Cortex, so a Stop or a crash leaves a run you can continue.
shots.alt: Cortex Lab builder Execution section with the Durable execution switch on and its hint, 'On by default'.

shots.caption: A model's page: capabilities, measured speed and spend, and how the harness adapts to it.
shots.alt: Cortex model page for a Claude model showing capabilities, speed, spend and the Calibration section, with notes on what applies only when learned calibration is on.

shots.caption: A tool that needs approval pauses the run and shows exactly what it will do. Nothing runs until you approve.
shots.alt: Cortex chat with a Waiting on you card for a file-write call showing its path and content parameters, with Approve, Deny and Dismiss buttons.

shots.caption: When a run ends early, the chat says why in plain words and offers Continue with more steps.
shots.alt: Cortex chat showing a run that stopped at its step limit: a 'Ran out of budget' card with the work already done, a note field, a More steps field and a Continue button.

shots.caption: The run view's Why it ended card: the cause, who is at fault, what to try, and the steps that decided it.
shots.alt: Cortex run view for a run that hit its iteration limit, with the Why it ended card open: cause, what to try, decisive steps, and the trace below.
shots.note: Diagnosis is the framework's (same engine as rax-diagnose cause) on a scripted run that was cut at its step limit. The per-loop speed readout (tok/s, first-token time) appears only when timing resolved, so it is hidden in the trace rows to keep the layout identical between runs.
